Latest Instagram News
World Challenge update: the team has arrived in Tofu and have enjoyed visiting the local market and making dinner!
Happy last day of term from Brooky, all faculty members and Mr McSweeney! We wish you all the best time over the summer Have fun! #theemmbrookschool #family
Don't forget the early finish tomorrow as the last day of term! All bus services have been rescheduled to earlier departure times. #theemmbrookschool
Posting this at half time to break the tension... Great fun at the colour run today! Well done to all students involved. Massive thank you to the PTA for organising
World Challenge update - they had an amazing welcome to Bazaruto Archipelago National Park where they will be learning about conservation and sand dunes. Reports are that they are having a seafood bbq, some beach football, and a small dip in the sea. Jealousy is a strong word.
Our Book of the Summer is Amari and the Night Brothers by B.B Alston. This exciting fantasy adventure follows Amari, a young girl who discovers a hidden world of magic while searching for her missing brother. Packed with mystery, humour and action, this is an excellent summer read for those who enjoy imaginative worlds and fast-paced stories. This is the first book in a popular series, so a great choice for encouraging reading over the summer holidays. Pick up the first book before we break up, or borrow one from your local library! #theemmbrookschool #ambition
The World Challenge expedition has made it to Mozambique! Good luck to all our adventurers #ambition
Sparx Maths - are you adding to the Maths house competition? Get those calculations working to earn SPARK XP and do as much as you can by the end of term to build towards the year group's goals to win first place! Good luck everyone! #theemmbrookschool #sparxmaths #ambition
Mr McSweeney has placed himself on duty by the ice cream van. Responsibilities for this post include; -Quality control -Product Tester -Benchmarking -Flake integrity assessor -Texture evaluation -Temperature compliance Always leading from the front. What a hero.
Are you joining our Sixth Form in September? Check out our website for more information: https://www.emmbrook.wokingham.sch.uk/page/?title=Sixth+Form&pid=6 #theemmbrooksixth #newstart #family
The Power of Music. Students were sensational on Wednesday evening at the Summer Concert, every performance was fantastic with such amazing quality of music in our community. It was a bittersweet moment however, as we said a musical goodbye to Mrs Wellman following her decision to retire after conducting the department for 12 years. Mrs Wellman has been a champion of the arts and developed such a strong community of musicians that all support each other regardless of instrument or age. Enjoy your retirement Mrs Wellman – it is very well earned!
Well done, everybody - keep it up! Ahead of Sports Day, here are the current totals.. wonder how it will change! #theemmbrookschool #ambition
"Keep exploring. Keep dreaming. Keep asking why. Don't settle for what you already know. Never stop believing in the power of your ideas, your imagination, and your hard work to change the world." #theemmbrookschool
July's Book of the Month is Amulet: The Stonekeeper by Kazu Kibuishi. This fantasy graphic novel launches a popular series filled with adventure and imaginative world-building. A great story to pick up if you've never read a graphic novel before. #theemmbrookschool #ambition
On Monday, students who demonstrated the highest levels of integrity across the term were rewarded with a visit to a mobile farm. They got to meet and interact with some cheeky goats, a fluffy baby donkey, sleepy pigs and more! A huge congratulations to all involved. #theemmbrookschool
We hope everyone has a fun few days at the leavers events for our Y11 & Y13. Good luck with your future adventures #theemmbrookschool #ambition #family

Open Evening & Tours
Save the date: Open Evening - Wednesday 16th September 2026
For information on our 6th Form open evening - click here
Tours will begin from the 10th of September (book here). Tours start at 9.00am and last around 90 minutes. You'll have the chance to see students and sixth formers actively engaged in lessons. The tour is led by Mr McSweeney and assisted by other senior leaders. It is a really good opportunity to see the school in full swing on a particularly normal day! We always advise having your children join the tour to start their familiarity early as we find it really helps with transition.
In previous years the tours have proved exceptionally popular and we will look to run more if demand is there.
We also have our Open Evening on the 16th September. The school will be open for tours or perusal from 6pm, you can choose to walk yourself around or have a student tour guide show you around. Mr McSweeney will be giving a talk at 6.00pm, 6.45pm and 7.30pm in which he will share the journey of the school and all our recent successes. Please click the time slot to book your place!
We are always very excited to showcase our school and the successes of our students and we can’t wait to show you our vision and values.
Looking for September 2027 new joiner information? Join our mailing list [click here] to be the first to hear about our opportunities for Year 6 pupils.
If you have any questions please email Mr Johnson (Assistant Headteacher responsible for transition) [email protected]
Message from Mr McSweeney (Headteacher)
Dear Parents, Carers and Students,
I am delighted to welcome you to The Emmbrook School. As a father of two (both at secondary school), I am acutely aware that choosing the right school is such a significant decision. This page will offer you a digital introduction to The Emmbrook.
Every September, I select a quote that sums up our ambition for the year ahead; this year
“The needs of the one outweigh the needs of the many" (Captain Kirk)
It’s important to me that we all work hard to support our vulnerable and disadvantaged students. If we are getting it right for them, everyone in the school benefits from the development of resources, focus and engagement.
I hope to meet you in one form or another in the coming months, via our tours, during the open evenings or at one of my online morning meetings for parents. Information regarding all these events will be released soon. In the meantime, if I can assist you personally, then please do contact me ([email protected]).
The schools in Wokingham are excellent, that should make this process easier, but somehow it makes it harder! Good luck with choosing the school that is right for you.

Any questions? Email Mr Constable (Head of Sixth Form) [email protected]

We Celebrate our Students’ Achievements - A-Level 2025
We are delighted to celebrate another year of exceptional A-Level results at The Emmbrook School. Following last year’s record-breaking performance, that placed our Sixth Form 8th nationally in 2024 (of 3665 state-funded schools and colleges) our students have once again demonstrated remarkable achievement by matching the record outcomes achieved last year.
This year’s results continue to reflect the dedication and hard work of our students, with strong outcomes across the board. This included one in ten grades achieved at A*, around a third A*-A and well over half of all grades at A*-B. The average grade achieved by all students was a B.
Subjects including Maths, Further Maths, Computer Science, Art, Criminology, and Psychology saw particularly impressive results, highlighting the breadth of academic excellence across our Sixth Form. There was also strong performance in the Sciences.
Nick McSweeney, Headteacher, shared, “We are incredibly proud of our students. Their commitment, resilience, and ambition have once again delivered outstanding results. To maintain such high standards after last year’s historic success is a testament to the strength of our school community. These achievements reflect the tireless efforts of our students, the expertise of our teachers, and the unwavering support of parents and carers.”
David Constable, Head of Sixth Form, commented, “The class of 2025 has continued the legacy of excellence at Emmbrook. Their results are a reflection of two years of hard work, focus, and determination. It has been a privilege to support them on their journey, and I am confident they will go on to achieve great things in the future.”
Pete Whitehouse, Assistant Headteacher responsible for Post-16, added, “I’m thrilled to see our students once again achieving such strong results. The consistency in high performance across subjects and grade boundaries shows the depth of talent and effort within this cohort. Congratulations to all of them for their well-earned success.”
Our students are now progressing to a wide range of exciting destinations. Many will be continuing their studies at top universities, including Oxford and Cambridge, while others are embarking on high-quality apprenticeships and vocational pathways. We celebrate every individual achievement and look forward to seeing our students thrive in the next chapter of their lives.

Careers Education (CEIAG)
Introduction
Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) at The Emmbrook School is a vital part of school life. All students will receive this as part of their learning here at the school. We are committed to providing the appropriate activities and experiences to enable students to make successful transitions from the start of Year 7, through Key Stages 4 and 5 and then on to further education, training programmes, apprenticeships or work.
The Emmbrook School CEIAG aims are:
· To allow students to make informed and considered choices at the end of all three key stages.
· To help and guide students to make transitions into new situations.
· To promote self-development in students including employability skills.
· To help students to value differences and diversity between people.
· To raise aspirations and make students aware of opportunities available to them.
· To provide guidance to all students in relation to decisions about options, further education and career choices, including apprenticeships.
Careers education should not just be seen as learning about jobs but also learning about work ethics, equipping students with skills (both hard and soft) for the workplace, ensuring transition occurs smoothly and helping to reduce barriers to entering the world of work.
Our careers provision at The Emmbrook is based on the GatsbyBenchmarks as recommended in the DfE’s Careers Strategy (December 2017) and the Statutory Guidance for Careers (January 2023).

For pupils in the ‘third key phase’ (year 12 to 13), particularly those that have not yet decided on their next steps, there are two more provider encounters available during this period, which are optional for pupils to attend.

In previous years the tours have proved exceptionally popular and we will look to run more if demand is there.
We also have our Open Evening on the 16th September. The school will be open for tours or perusal from 6pm, you can choose to walk yourself around or have a student tour guide show you around. Message from Mr McSweeney (Headteacher)
Dear Parents, Carers and Students,
I am delighted to welcome you to The Emmbrook School. As a father of two (both at secondary school), I am acutely aware that choosing the right school is such a significant decision. This page will offer you a digital introduction to The Emmbrook.
Every September, I select a quote that sums up our ambition for the year ahead; this year
“The needs of the one outweigh the needs of the many" (Captain Kirk)
It’s important to me that we all work hard to support our vulnerable and disadvantaged students. If we are getting it right for them, everyone in the school benefits from the development of resources, focus and engagement.
I hope to meet you in one form or another in the coming months, via our tours, during the open evenings or at one of my online morning meetings for parents. Information regarding all these events will be released soon. In the meantime, if I can assist you personally, then please do contact me ([email protected]).
The schools in Wokingham are excellent, that should make this process easier, but somehow it makes it harder! Good luck with choosing the school that is right for you.

Mrs Ridsdale Message:
A key aspect of my role in school is being the designated safeguarding lead. This includes creating a culture where all members of staff at the Emmbrook School are committed to ensuring our students are safe and are promoting and supporting the welfare of all of our students. Alongside myself we have a specific safeguarding team who support in ensuring this happens day to day. All staff receive specific training at the start of the academic year and then this is supported weekly with key safeguarding topics or areas are being shared. This ensures are staff are fully equipped with the knowledge and skills to be able to identify concerns and have robust process and systems in place to support us to provide support for students where needed. We utilise both internal and external resources, strategies and interventions to implement the right support which will in turn positively impact our student’s welfare and well-being.

It is important to add we continually reflect and review what we do and also identify what we can be doing more of to ensure we provide outstanding provisions to support all of our students.
Safeguarding is everybody’s responsibility and we are committed as a school to ensure we provide a school environment where all of our students feel safe and happy to enable them to thrive and flourish during their 7-year educational journey at The Emmbrook School.

IF YOU HAVE A CONCERN ABOUT YOUR CHILD OR SOMEBODY ELSE IN THE SCHOOL COMMUNITY – WHAT TO DO?
If you have concerns about your child or somebody in the school community please do not hesitate to contact a member of the safeguarding team via main reception (01189784406) or on the automated email links above. As a school we have a team safeguarding email that is accessible by all which is listed below:
If you wish, you can telephone Wokingham Children’s Services (0118 9088002) for advice without identifying the child.
Advice for parents from YoungMinds can be found here: https://www.youngminds.org.uk/parent/
IF WE HAVE A CONCERN ABOUT YOUR CHILD – WHAT WE DO?
If we are concerned that your child may be at risk of abuse or neglect, we must follow the procedures in our safeguarding policy. You can look at the policy on the school website. The procedures have been written to protect all students. They comply with our statutory responsibilities and are designed to support students, families and staff. The procedures are based on the principle that the welfare of the child is the most important consideration.
In almost all circumstances, we will talk to you about our concerns and we will also tell you if we feel we must refer our concerns to children’s social care. We will ask your consent to make a referral, but in some circumstances, we may need to make the referral against your wishes. We will only do this if we genuinely believe that this is the best way to protect your child, and the fact that you did not consent to the referral will be recorded.
Child protection is a very sensitive issue and it raises many questions as well as a range of strong emotions. We will do everything we can to support our students and you can be assured that any action we take will be in the best interests of your child.
